steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Roman society was rigidly hierarchical with patricians at the top and slaves at the bottom

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Patricians were the aristocratic families who held political power and owned vast estates

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Plebeians were the common citizens — farmers, traders, artisans and labourers

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Conflict of the Orders gradually gave plebeians more political rights over centuries

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link social structure to political power — the two were inseparable in Rome The patron-client system is the key to understanding how Roman society actually functioned Use specific examples of social hierarchy in action, not just definitions Compare the theory of the social structure with the reality of individual experience Remember that women, though formally excluded from politics, wielded significant informal influence
